newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds churn in narrow range.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds churn in narrow range.

text.p: *Australian bonds churned in a narrow range during a listless trading session in the absence of major data and due to Monday's U.S. holiday.
*U.S. faces key inflation data later this week.
Australian bonds churned in a narrow range during a slow trading session with little to inspire the market from their current low yield levels.

A holiday in the U.S. today for Veteran's Day virtually guaranteed a thin day locally with no major local data due out, and with all the action expected towards second half of the week when the U.S. gets its key PPI and CPI reports.
The Federal Open Market Committee also meets on Wednesday, but no change in policy is expected to be endorsed.
Local yields remain close to their 32-month lows following last week's RBA monetary policy easing to 6.5 percent.
The 10-year bond yield eased to around 7.17 percent at one stage last week and could ease to 7.0 percent, but beyond that analysts feel it would need a further policy easing.

Today's release of September housing finance showed a 5.8 percent, much in line with expectations. In terms of policy settings, it has no implications and had no market impact, said John Peters, senior economist at Westpac.

"The overall picture of housing finance continues to be distorted by the ongoing refinancing war," Peters said, adding that while it confirmed the housing market had troughed, it was not signalling any substantive rebound.

Yield margins narrowed to New Zealand debt which came under pressure after comments by RBNZ governor Don Brash warning of problems on the fiscal front and urged spending restraint to curb the N.Z. dollar. The 10-year N.Z. yield went back to a premium over Australia for the first time since mid-October.
